title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook (v2)
author: Avery Chen
content:
Purpose

This consolidated playbook defines Redwood Inference's operating procedures for hiring, pre-boarding/onboarding, ongoing performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, recruiters, engineering managers, and HR partners.

Scope & Owners

- Applies to: full-time employees, contractors, and interns in North America and Europe. Region-specific notes are flagged inline.
- Core owners: People Ops (process design and ATS hygiene), Hiring Manager (role definition and interview decisions), Recruiter (candidate experience), IT (access provisioning), Finance & Legal (comp and policy approvals).

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Goal: hire high-quality candidates with an inclusive, consistent candidate experience. Targets: time-to-fill <= 45 days, offer acceptance >= 70%, diverse slate >= 30% when feasible.

Requisition & approval
- Manager opens requisition in Workday (or People Ops Google form if Workday unavailable). Required: title, team, level/band, hiring rationale, must-have skills, remote/onsite expectation, proposed range, and hiring owner.
- People Ops verifies headcount and budget; Finance approves band exceptions. SLA: acknowledgement within 48 business hours.

Sourcing & initial screen
- Recruiter builds sourcing plan (referrals, LinkedIn, university partners, agencies for niche roles).
- Recruiter screen: 30 minutes to confirm interest, compensation baseline, legal work eligibility, and high-level fit. Use standard screen checklist.
- All interviewers must complete a structured scorecard within 24 hours (rubric: 0-4).

Interview loop & rubric
- Typical engineering IC loop: Recruiter Screen -> Hiring Manager (30 min) -> Technical Pairing/Exercise -> System Design (senior) -> Behavioral/PRD-fit -> Hiring Committee.
- Panels should include at least one interviewer outside the direct team. Use 0-4 rubric: 0 = no evidence, 1 = limited, 2 = meets, 3 = exceeds, 4 = exceptional. Document concrete examples.

Hiring Committee (HC) & decision
- HC members: Hiring Manager, 2+ senior peers, Tech Lead, Recruiter/People Ops.
- Decision: majority recommendation required. For borderline cases HC may request an additional loop or take a conditional offer. Record decision in ATS and notify candidate within 48 hours.

Offer & negotiation
- Offer packet includes: offer letter, total comp breakdown (base/equity/bonus if applicable), benefits summary, start date options, and next steps for onboarding.
- Approval flow: Hiring Manager -> People Ops Lead -> Finance (for exceptions) -> Legal (if non-standard). Target sign-off: 3 business days.
- Negotiation: managers must stay within approved bands unless an exception is approved; People Ops provides market context.

Background & reference checks
- Initiate background check after verbal acceptance (vendor: GoodHire or region equivalent).
- Run references for senior and customer-facing hires; People Ops can assist or conduct them.

Candidate experience & declines
- Close candidates promptly with a respectful note and constructive feedback where possible. Record rejection reasons in ATS for reporting.

2) Onboarding & pre-boarding

Goal: accelerate new-hire productivity and alignment with clear 30/60/90 milestones.

Pre-boarding (1-2 weeks prior)
- People Ops: welcome email, new-hire paperwork, benefits enrollment window, and first-day logistics.
- IT: create accounts in Okta, G Suite, Slack, Jira, Confluence; order and ship laptop and peripherals.
- Manager: send team welcome, confirm day-1 agenda, assign buddy, and calendar first-week 1:1s.

Day 1
- Morning: company orientation (People Ops), security training, benefits overview.
- Afternoon: manager-led role overview, immediate access/setup, lightweight onboarding assignment, and intro to buddy.
- Checkpoint: confirm all access provisioned; escalate to IT runbook if not.

Week 1 & 30/60/90
- Week 1 tasks: complete mandatory trainings (Security & Privacy, Code of Conduct), product orientation, and first mini-assignment.
- 30 days: contributor on small tasks, completed core training, met cross-functional partners.
- 60 days: deliver a measurable project or feature, own recurring tasks, initial performance check-in.
- 90 days: full contribution to team goals and 90-day review (manager documents outcomes and next steps).

Remote onboarding considerations
- Ship equipment >= 5 business days before start. Record live intro sessions and stagger live events by timezone.

3) Performance, feedback & career growth

Cadence & inputs
- Continuous feedback encouraged; weekly or biweekly 1:1s documented in notes.
- Quarterly: team OKR planning and check-ins.
- Annual review: goal-setting, self-assessment, peer feedback, manager assessment, calibration, compensation decision. People Ops publishes timeline each cycle.

Manager guidance on feedback
- Use SBI (Situation-Behavior-Impact) and focus on observable actions and concrete next steps. Document feedback and follow up.

Promotions & level changes
- Promotion packet should include manager justification, impact examples (with links), peer endorsements, and updated role expectations.
- People Ops coordinates compensation/title changes and schedules calibration. Promotions normally align to quarterly comp cycles; out-of-cycle requires CFO approval.

Performance Improvement Plans (PIP)
- PIPs are used after coaching attempts fail. Typical steps: document gaps and success criteria, review with People Ops and Legal, deliver PIP with timeline (60-90 days), weekly check-ins, and document outcomes. PIP records are confidential.

4) Manager playbook (practical checklists)

Hiring manager checklist
- Pre-posting: write a concise role brief, align level/band with People Ops, propose interview panel.
- During loop: ensure interviewers have scorecards and candidate context; review scorecards within 24 hours.
- Post-decision: support offer extension, prepare onboarding plan and 30/60/90 goals.

First 90 days manager checklist
- Day 0-7: welcome, confirm access, assign buddy, set first deliverable.
- Week 2-4: confirm training completion, introduce stakeholders, run early feedback session.
- Month 1-3: track progress vs goals, set development objectives, conduct 90-day review.

One-on-one & career conversations
- Typical agenda: wins, blockers, goals, feedback, and a 10-20 minute development conversation.
- Use competency framework to map levels and co-create a 6-12 month growth plan.

Offboarding checklist
- Manager: collect outstanding work, ensure knowledge transfer, archive docs, schedule exit interview with People Ops. IT revokes non-admin access on last working day; for security-sensitive roles revoke within 24 hours.

5) Policies, tools & compliance

- Mandatory trainings: Security & Privacy, Data Handling (engineers with customer data), and Code of Conduct.
- Tools: Greenhouse (ATS), Workday (HRIS), Okta (SSO), BambooHR/ADP (payroll by region), GoodHire (background checks).
- Legal & security reviews are required for roles with data access or external-facing responsibilities.

6) Templates (copy/paste)

Offer email (brief)
Subject: Redwood Inference — Final Offer for [Role]
Body: Hi [Candidate],
We're excited to offer you the role of [Role] on the [Team]. Attached is the formal offer letter and comp summary. Proposed start date: [Date]. Please reach out with questions.

PIP header template
- Objective: [Measurable outcome]
- Timeline: [Start] — [End] (60-90 days)
- Success criteria: [3 measurable items]
- Manager support: [Weekly 1:1s, resources, training]

30/60/90 example (short)
- 30 days: complete core training and deliver a small task.
- 60 days: own a small feature and demonstrate cross-team collaboration.
- 90 days: independently deliver a medium project and present outcomes.

7) KPIs, reporting & escalations

KPIs tracked monthly (People Ops dashboard)
- Time-to-fill, Offer acceptance rate, New-hire 90-day retention, Ramp time to baseline productivity, Training completion rate.

Escalations
- For urgent hiring or compensation exceptions: email people-ops@redwood.ai with subject [Escalation: Role - Team].
- For legal, security, or data residency questions loop in Legal or Security leads.

Appendices & links
- A: Interview scorecard template (Confluence link)
- B: Level competency framework (Confluence link)
- C: Compensation bands & approval flow (Finance doc link)

Document maintenance
- Owner: People Ops (Avery Chen). Review cadence: annual or when policy changes. Major changes require cross-functional review (Engineering Managers, SRE, Finance, Legal).

End of playbook
